findings.title: The zero-failure bounds and counted coverage ignore whether counted pairs actually passed
findings.detail: diagnostics() counts a pair as 'counted' when F1 did not exclude it. It then reports pooled_zero_failure_bound95 = 1 - 0.05^(1/n_counted), plus per-type and clustered bounds, whether or not those pairs met the 2 % agreement. A zero-failure bound is only valid when there are zero failures. When A1 is met the numbers are right: no pair can be excluded and every |d| is at most 2 %. On any other outcome the metric reports a 'zero-failure' bound while a failure is present.
findings.evidence: Synthetic harness through assemble/criteria/diagnostics with 4 pairs, one of them (P3) 4 % off FastHenry: A1 = 0.0385 (not met), but n_counted = 4, pooled_zero_failure_bound95 = 0.527 and clustered = 0.776 are still reported.
findings.suggested_check: Compute the bounds only over counted pairs within A1's threshold, or label them 'valid only if A1 is met' in the metric and solve.json.

findings.title: A deterministic discretisation band is recorded as a 95 % confidence interval
findings.detail: stage_solve passes ratio_band(...), i.e. [max(0, |d| - u), |d| + u] built from the solvers' discretisation estimates, as ci= to run.metric. run.metric's default level is 0.95, so result.json will show A1, K1 and K2 with a '95 % CI' that is not a statistical interval. The criteria use point values (uncertainty: point), so no verdict changes, but a reader or a later claim could misread it.
findings.evidence: e004_run.py stage_solve: run.metric('max_ratio_diff_vs_fasthenry', crit['A1'], ci=b1 ...), with no level argument; mfos/evidence.py metric(..., level=0.95).
findings.suggested_check: Move the band into solve.json diagnostics, or record it with an explicit non-statistical label instead of the default 0.95 level.

findings.title: The job-list deliverable is stale against the committed probe record
findings.detail: vm_jobs_fasthenry.json marks gen2_0__fh_g3 as precond_probe 'vm_first: not probed locally'. Yet fh_probe.json has a local probe of the identical deck (same deck_sha256 83e9d2b10289…) with result 'timeout' (1800 s, 770 MB, never reached 'Calling gmres'). dev_fh_plan would have copied that result, so the plan was written before the probe record and never regenerated.
findings.evidence: Deck-hash comparison: gen2_0__fh_g1 matches (past_preconditioner, calibration 15.2x applied); gen2_0__fh_g3 matches by sha, but the plan shows the default vm_first text instead of 'timeout'.
findings.suggested_check: Re-run `e004_run.py --dev-fh-plan` and confirm every probed deck's precond_probe equals its fh_probe.json result.

findings.title: Coverage after exclusion does not apply O004's 6 % effect rule, and the covered ratio range can include rows from pairs that are not counted
findings.detail: O004 scope_in says a move type is covered only if one of its counted pairs has |1 - r| >= 6 % at L1. diagnostics() reports only per-type counts, without re-applying that rule after exclusion. covered_range_fh_finest takes r_fh from every non-excluded row, so a pair excluded at one frequency still adds its other-frequency ratio. This has no effect on a pass, because A1 cannot be met with any exclusion; it only affects the INCONCLUSIVE diagnostics.
findings.evidence: e004_run.py diagnostics(): per_type has pairs/counted/excluded/bound only; rfh = [r['r_fh'] for r in pr if not r['excluded_f1'] ...] works row by row, not pair by pair.
findings.suggested_check: Re-apply the coverage rule (min over FK of |1 - r_L1| >= 0.06) to counted pairs, and build the covered range from counted pairs only.

findings.title: A tight FastHenry memory cap can turn a mis-projection into a missing judged value and an INVALID run
findings.detail: mem_cap_mb is set to 1.3 x (31.1 kB x exporter filaments), a linear fit from P4's 25k–102k-filament runs. It is applied to the judged references' k2 decks (330k–431k filaments) and to F7(a)'s Case 4 k2 decks (about 1.17M filaments). The adapter kills a run above the cap and does not retry, so a missing finest value makes the run INVALID unless K1 fires, and that burns the sealed pairs (decision_if_fail). The VM has 108 GB of usable memory, but the cap is 17 GB for 2R's k2 deck. The spec says F7(a) recalibrates the time rule before registration; it says nothing about refitting kb_per_filament.
findings.evidence: vm_jobs_fasthenry.json e004_cost_plan: 2D_Case_2R k2_nh5 has 430,924 filaments and mem_proj 17.4 GB; fasthenry_run.py lines 215-216 kill above mem_cap_mb, and line 315 does not retry killed_memory.
findings.suggested_check: Before registration, refit the sizing rule from F7(a)'s measured peaks, or set the judged runs' cap from VM headroom rather than from the projection.

findings.title: gci_capped on the 3 / 5 / 9 thickness ladder assumes a refinement ratio of 2
findings.detail: FastHenry's thickness term adds gci_capped(f3, f5, f9), whose formula assumes r = 2. The ladder's actual ratios are 1.67 and 1.8, so at the order cap p = 1 it understates f9's error by up to 1/(1.8 - 1) = 1.25x, roughly cancelling Roache's 1.25 safety factor. O004 freezes this estimator, so the code follows the spec.
findings.evidence: fh_terms(): fin = gci_capped(*thk) with thk = (nh 3, 5, 9); gci_capped uses |d2| / (2^p - 1).
findings.suggested_check: Report the r = 1.8 form beside the frozen value in the F7(a) results.

findings.title: The smoke run reports freeze_hashes_match = false at this commit
findings.detail: The smoke registration recorded freeze_hashes_match false (smoke records it and does not refuse). The likely cause is that this review checkout is a single 'review snapshot' commit, so the frozen commit 3f60b2f4 is not among HEAD's ancestors. That was not confirmed. If the cause is instead a hash mismatch on the real branch, registration would refuse.
findings.evidence: Smoke output: checks.freeze_hashes_match false; git log shows a single commit 0eb19df 'review snapshot'.
findings.suggested_check: Run `e004_run.py --print-freeze` on the real task branch and confirm it matches config.freeze.
